question: A certain sum becomes 4 times itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 12 times itself at the same rate?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes n₁ times in T₁ years and n₂ times in T₂ years at the same simple interest rate, we use the direct ratio:

(n₁ − 1) / T₁ = (n₂ − 1) / T₂

⇒ (4 − 1) / 8 = (12 − 1) / T₂

⇒ 3 / 8 = 11 / T₂

⇒ T₂ = 88 / 3 = 29 ¹/₃ years

**∴ The correct answer is 29 ¹/₃ years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A sum becomes 4 times itself in 8 years at simple interest.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Amount (A) = P + SI
